title: Semantic-Aware Motion Encoding for Topology-Agnostic Character Animation
claim: One shared encoder-decoder bridges different skeleton topologies through a common semantic space, enabling retargeting to unseen characters without paired data.
layout: Single panel, top-to-bottom flow, with a central semantic-space box and dashed arrows
description: The figure is a single flow diagram. At top left, a rendered source human motion (three poses) and a 24-joint source skeleton feed into a blue trapezoid Encoder. The encoder outputs yellow motion-feature slabs that connect to a blue manifold surface labeled Topology-Agnostic Motion Manifold, with an orange trajectory drawn on it. A black line carries the feature down and splits left and right to two Shared Decoders. In the center, a dashed peach box called Shared Semantic Space holds tokens such as <Semantic: Left Knee>, <Semantic: Left Leg> and <Semantic: Head>. Orange dashed arrows link a joint on the source skeleton and joints on the 27-joint and 52-joint target skeletons to these tokens. The decoders output rendered motions of a cartoon mouse (left) and a cat (right) at the bottom. Joint counts are in red. The eye goes first to the encoder and manifold at top, then to the central semantic box.
caption: Zero-shot cross-species retargeting via a topology-agnostic motion manifold. Our method encodes source motion into a unified latent space, leveraging a shared semantic space to bridge disparate skeletal structures. The encoded features are then decoded into motion for diverse target topologies. This representation enables robust zero-shot generalization to heterogeneous skeletons, even without paired training data.
abstract: Generalizing motion representation across diverse characters remains challenging due to significant topological variations in skeletal structures across datasets and species, which hinder the development of scalable generative models. To bridge this gap, we propose a Semantic-Aware Topology-Agnostic framework that learns a unified latent manifold shared by disparate species. Unlike methods relying on fixed hierarchies or rigid padding strategies, our approach leverages a semantic modulation mechanism to align functional joint correspondences, thereby decoupling motion from topology. This design enables the construction of a continuous, generative-friendly motion space from large-scale, unaligned raw BVH data. Experiments on human and animal datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and supports downstream text-to-motion tasks. Notably, the model enables zero-shot cross-species retargeting without paired data. Code and demos are available at: https://github.com/zzysteve/SATA
